genesis: God speaks a world into being in six days and rests on the seventh. Humankind is made in his image.
The garden, a river, a helper, a tree, and a limit: do not eat of that one.
The serpent, the eating, shame, blame, a curse, and the way back guarded.
Cain kills Abel. A mark, a city, Lamech’s boast. Adam’s line continues through Seth.
From Adam to Noah: a genealogy, and Enoch who walked with God.
The earth is filled with violence. Noah finds favour. An ark is commanded.
The flood comes. All flesh with breath of life dies, except those in the ark.
The waters recede. A raven, a dove, dry ground, an altar, a pleasing aroma.
A covenant and a bow in the cloud. Blood is forbidden as food. Noah’s vineyard and Canaan’s curse.
The table of nations: Japheth, Ham, Shem, and how the earth was divided.
Babel: one language, a tower, a scattering. Shem’s line down to Abram.
The Lord calls Abram. A land, a people, a blessing for the families of the earth. Egypt, a lie about Sarai.
Abram and Lot separate. Abram is promised the land as far as he can see.
Abram rescues Lot from four kings. Melchizedek brings bread and wine. Abram takes no spoil.
A covenant by cut animals. Abram believes, and it is counted as righteousness. Four hundred years of sojourning named.
Hagar conceives Ishmael and flees. The Lord names the child and sends her back.
Circumcision as the sign. Abram becomes Abraham, Sarai Sarah. A son is promised this time next year.
Three visitors. Sarah laughs. Abraham bargains for Sodom: fifty down to ten.
Sodom and Gomorrah burn. Lot is pulled out. A cave, and Moab and Ammon from a drunken night.
Abraham and Abimelech: another wife-sister lie, a dream, a treaty at Beer-sheba.
Isaac is born. Hagar and Ishmael are sent away. God hears the boy. A treaty with Abimelech.
The binding of Isaac. A ram in the thicket. The Lord will provide. Rebekah’s family is named.
Sarah dies. Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah — the first plot of promised land he owns.
A wife for Isaac: Rebekah at the well, a long journey, love in the field at evening.
Abraham dies. Ishmael’s twelve princes. Esau and Jacob wrestle in the womb; a birthright sold for stew.
Isaac in Gerar, wells reopened, a treaty. Esau’s Hittite wives make life bitter.
Jacob steals the blessing with a goatskin. Esau weeps and plans murder. Jacob flees to Haran.
A stone pillow at Bethel: a ladder, a promise, a vow. If God will be with me.
Jacob, Laban, Leah, Rachel. Fourteen years for two wives. The unloved wife is given children.
More sons, a mandrake bargain, speckled flocks. Jacob prospers and Laban’s face changes.
Jacob flees with household and household gods. Laban pursues. A covenant at Galeed.
Jacob wrestles until daybreak and is named Israel. He limps into the morning.
Esau comes with four hundred. They weep, and part. Jacob builds a booth at Succoth.
Dinah is violated. Simeon and Levi slaughter Shechem. Jacob is afraid of the Canaanites.
Back to Bethel. Rachel dies bearing Benjamin. Reuben’s sin. Isaac dies. Esau and Jacob bury him.
Esau’s descendants and the chiefs of Edom, in the land before Israel has a king.
Joseph’s dreams, a coat, a pit, a sale to Ishmaelites. The brothers lie to Jacob.
Judah and Tamar: a widow’s claim, a scarlet thread, Perez in the line that will run to David.
Joseph in Potiphar’s house. A lie, a prison, and the Lord still with him.
Cupbearer and baker dream. Joseph interprets. The cupbearer forgets him two years.
Pharaoh’s dreams. Joseph is raised to feed Egypt. Seven plenty, seven famine. Asenath, two sons.
Brothers come for grain. Joseph tests them. Simeon is bound. Jacob will not send Benjamin.
The grain is gone. Judah stands surety. Benjamin goes. Joseph weeps in another room.
The silver cup. Judah offers himself for the boy. Joseph can bear it no longer.
Joseph reveals himself. You sold me; God sent me. Send for my father. Wagons from Pharaoh.
Jacob comes to Egypt, sacrifices at Beer-sheba, is told not to fear. Seventy persons. Goshen.
Jacob meets Pharaoh. The famine is severe. Joseph buys land for Pharaoh. Israel settles.
Jacob blesses Ephraim and Manasseh, the younger ahead of the older again. God be with you.
Jacob’s last words over the twelve: Judah’s sceptre, Joseph’s bow. A burial charge for Canaan.
Jacob is buried at Machpelah. The brothers fear; Joseph weeps. You meant evil; God meant good. Joseph’s bones will go up.
exodus: Israel multiplies. A new king who did not know Joseph. Midwives who fear God. Moses in the reeds.
Moses kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian, marries Zipporah. God hears the groaning.
The bush that burns and is not consumed. I AM WHO I AM. Moses is sent with signs.
Moses objects; Aaron is given. A night circumcision. First audience with Pharaoh.
Bricks without straw. The officers of Israel cry out. Moses complains to the Lord.
God restates his name and the promise. Genealogy of Moses and Aaron. I will redeem you.
Staffs become serpents. Water becomes blood. Pharaoh’s heart is hard.
Frogs, gnats, flies. The magicians fail. Goshen is spared.
Livestock, boils, hail. Some of Pharaoh’s servants begin to fear the word of the Lord.
Locusts, darkness that can be felt. Pharaoh bargains and breaks.
The last plague announced. One more blow: the firstborn.
Passover night: lamb, blood on the door, unleavened bread. Israel is driven out.
Unleavened bread as a statute. The firstborn belong to the Lord. Joseph’s bones go up.
The sea. A pillar of cloud and fire. Pharaoh pursues. The waters return.
The song of the sea. Miriam dances. Bitter water at Marah made sweet.
Manna and quail. Sabbath in the gathering. A jar kept for a memorial.
Water from the rock at Rephidim. Amalek fought with hands held up.
Jethro advises judges. Moses cannot hear every case alone.
Sinai. A kingdom of priests. Thunder, a boundary, the people tremble.
The ten words. An altar of earth. I have talked with you from heaven.
The book of the covenant: servants, injury, property, justice at the gate.
Theft, damage, social law, the sojourner. You shall not oppress.
Justice, sabbaths, three feasts a year. An angel on the way. Do not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.
The blood of the covenant. Seventy elders eat and see God. Moses on the mountain forty days.
The tabernacle pattern: offering, ark, table, lampstand.
Curtains, frames, veil — a holy place that can move with the camp.
Bronze altar, court, oil for the lamp that must not go out.
The priests’ garments: ephod, breastpiece, Urim and Thummim, a crown Holy to the Lord.
Consecration of priests. Daily offerings. I will dwell among the people of Israel.
Incense altar, census tax, basin, anointing oil, incense.
Bezalel and Oholiab filled with the Spirit for craft. Sabbath as covenant sign. Two tablets.
The golden calf. Tablets broken. Levites, a plague, Moses’ plea.
A tent outside the camp. My presence will go with you. Moses sees glory from the cleft.
New tablets. The Lord, a God merciful and gracious. Moses’ face shines.
Sabbath restated. The people bring more than enough for the tent.
The work of the tent: curtains and frames, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The ark, table, lampstand, incense altar made of gold.
The burnt-offering altar, basin, court, and the bronze of the census.
The priests’ garments finished. Moses inspects all the work and blesses them.
The tent is raised. Glory fills it. Cloud by day, fire by night. When it lifts, they move.
leviticus: Burnt offering: a life wholly given, a pleasing aroma.
Grain offering: flour, oil, frankincense — the work of hands.
Peace offering: fellowship, fat for the Lord, meat shared.
Sin offering for priest, congregation, leader, anyone. Unintentional sin still costs.
Guilt offering: restitution plus a fifth, for holy things and neighbour-harm.
Priestly portions and the holiness of the altar fire that must not go out.
What may be eaten from offerings, and what must not leave the court.
Aaron and his sons consecrated. Blood on ear, thumb, and toe.
The eighth day. Fire from the Lord consumes the offering. The people shout and fall.
Nadab and Abihu offer strange fire and die. Distinguishing holy and common is not optional.
Clean and unclean creatures. You shall be holy, for I am holy.
Childbirth and the days of purification.
Skin disease: diagnosis, isolation, the priest as public officer of holiness.
Cleansing of the leper: two birds, water, blood, oil.
Houses and garments with disease. Discharges from the body. Isolation and return.
The Day of Atonement: two goats, one for the Lord, one for Azazel. Blood in the holy place.
Blood is life; it belongs on the altar, not in the pot as food.
Sexual prohibitions. The land will vomit out what Canaan practised.
You shall be holy: neighbour, poor, deaf, blind, justice, love your neighbour as yourself.
Penalties. Molech. Mediums. Priests’ holiness and whom they may marry.
The high priest, blemishes, who may eat holy food.
Acceptable offerings: without blemish. The Lord is not to be given leftovers.
Sabbaths, Passover, firstfruits, weeks, trumpets, the Day, booths.
Lamp, bread of the presence, a blasphemer stoned. Eye for eye in court, not in the street.
Sabbath year and jubilee. The land is the Lord’s. Kin redeem. No perpetual underclass if the law is kept.
Blessings for loyalty, curses for refusal — exile named in advance.
Vows, valuations, firstborn, tithe. Leviticus ends in the wilderness of Sinai, still at the tent.
numbers: First census of fighting men. The camp ordered around the tent.
The tribes in their places. Judah on the east, nearest the sunrise.
Levites instead of the firstborn. Gershon, Kohath, Merari.
Kohathites carry the holy things — covered, not touched.
Purity in the camp. Restitution. A test for suspected adultery.
The Nazirite vow. Aaron’s blessing: the Lord bless you and keep you.
Offerings at the dedication of the altar, tribe by tribe, twelve days.
The lamps set up. Levites cleansed and given to Aaron.
A second Passover for the unclean. Cloud and fire say when they camp and when they move.
Silver trumpets. They leave Sinai. Hobab is asked to be eyes in the wilderness.
Complaint, fire, quail, a plague. Moses’ spirit shared with seventy. The grave of greed.
Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses. Miriam’s leprosy, seven days outside.
Twelve spies. A good land, giants. We are not able. Caleb and Joshua dissent.
The people refuse. Forty years. The spies who brought a bad report die. A rash attack fails.
Offerings in the land-to-come. A Sabbath-breaker stoned. Tassels on garments.
Korah, Dathan, Abiram. The earth opens. Censers beaten into a covering for the altar.
Aaron’s rod buds. A warning against approaching the sanctuary uncalled.
Priests’ and Levites’ portions. The covenant of salt.
The red heifer. Water for impurity after death.
Miriam dies. Water from the rock; Moses strikes and is barred from the land. Edom refuses passage. Aaron dies on Hor.
King of Arad. The bronze serpent. Sihon and Og. The journey east of the Jordan.
Balak hires Balaam to curse Israel. A donkey sees the angel Balaam will not.
Balaam blesses instead of cursing. How can I curse whom God has not cursed?
Balaam’s last oracles. A star out of Jacob. Balak’s anger.
Baal-peor. Phinehas. A plague stopped by zeal. Midian to be struck.
Second census on the plains of Moab. The first generation is gone.
Zelophehad’s daughters. Inheritance for women when there is no son. Moses will not enter; Joshua will.
Daily, sabbath, and monthly offerings. Passover and weeks restated.
Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, booths — the calendar for a people about to be farmers.
Vows of men and women. When a father or husband may annul.
War with Midian. Balaam dies. Spoil counted and purified.
Reuben and Gad want the east bank. Moses grants it if they will fight across the Jordan.
Stages from Egypt to Moab. A travel log of forty years.
Borders of the land. Leaders named to divide it.
Levitical cities and pastureland. Six cities of refuge for the manslayer.
Zelophehad’s daughters must marry within the tribe so the inheritance stays. Numbers ends in Moab, in sight of the land.
deuteronomy: Moses begins: what God did from Horeb to this day. Go in and take possession.
The wilderness years. Edom, Moab, Ammon left unfought. Sihon taken.
Og of Bashan. Land east of the Jordan for two and a half tribes. Moses pleads to enter and is refused.
A charge to keep the statutes. No images. The Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath.
The ten words restated. The Lord talked with you face to face at the mountain.
Hear, O Israel. The Lord is one. Love him with all your heart. Teach the children. Bind the words.
Drive out the nations. The Lord did not set his love on you because you were many, but because he loved you.
Remember the manna. Man does not live by bread alone. Do not say my power got this wealth.
Not because of your righteousness — you are a stiff-necked people. The calf remembered.
New tablets. Circumcise your heart. The Lord executes justice for the orphan and the widow.
Therefore love and obey. A blessing and a curse set before them on Gerizim and Ebal.
The place the Lord will choose. Do not copy the nations’ worship. Tithe and rejoicing.
Do not listen to the dreamer, the family member, or the city that says, let us go after other gods.
Clean and unclean food. You are a people holy to the Lord. Tithe of produce.
The seventh year release of debts. Open your hand to the poor. Hebrew servants go free.
Passover, weeks, booths. Justice in the gates. Three times a year every male appears.
Hard cases to the priests. A king who must copy this law and not multiply horses, wives, or silver.
The priests’ due. No diviners. A prophet like Moses from among you.
Cities of refuge for the manslayer. Boundary stones. Two or three witnesses. A malicious witness.
War: who may go home, who is spared, the tree that is not a man. Cities that make peace, and those that do not.
Unsolved murder, captive women, inheritance of the firstborn, a rebellious son, a hanged man is accursed.
A neighbour’s ox, mixed cloth, tassels, slander about a bride, sexual law.
Those excluded from the assembly. Uncleanness in camp. Vows. Grapes and grain for the poor.
Divorce, pledges, wages, justice for the sojourner, orphan, widow.
Forty lashes. The ox treading. A brother’s name raised. Honest weights. Amalek remembered.
Firstfruits and the story: a wandering Aramean was my father. Tithe of the third year.
Gerizim and Ebal. The words of this law written on plastered stones. Twelve curses.
Blessings if you obey; curses if you will not — graphic, and aimed at the heart.
The covenant in Moab as well as at Horeb. Secret things belong to the Lord; revealed things to us.
When all these things come upon you in exile, return. The word is very near you. Choose life.
Moses and Joshua commissioned. Write this song as a witness. I know how rebellious you are.
The song of Moses: the Rock, the people’s folly, vengeance and mercy, nations called to rejoice.
Moses blesses the tribes. There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your help.
Moses dies on Nebo. The Lord buries him. Joshua is full of the spirit of wisdom. No prophet like Moses — yet.
